purpose: Enalapril is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to treat heart failure and to protect your kidneys, especially if you have diabetes. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps your heart and blood vessels stay healthier longer.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to squeeze tight, which raises your blood pressure. Enalapril blocks the enzyme that makes this chemical, so your blood vessels can relax and open up. When your blood vessels are more relaxed, your heart doesn't have to work as hard, and your blood pressure comes down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a dry, nagging cough that doesn't go away — this happens in some people and is the most frequent reason folks switch medications. You may also notice dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly, mild headache, or feeling a bit tired. Some people experience a slight increase in potassium levels in their blood.
warnings: Do NOT take enalapril if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm or even be fatal to an unborn baby. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat — this is a rare but serious reaction called angioedema. Avoid taking potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without asking your doctor first, and let all your healthcare providers know you are taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 5 mg once a day, and your doctor may slowly increase it up to 40 mg per day taken once or twice daily. For heart failure, doses are typically lower to start and adjusted carefully. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes, with or without food, and try to take it at the same time each day to keep it working consistently.
